level.title: Elementary: city, travel, routines, health
goals: Find your way around a Brazilian city
Talk about past trips with pretérito perfeito
Describe routines, health, and future plans

lessons.title: Around the city (estou no/na)
lessons.learn: Location uses ESTAR: ESTOU EM CASA (I am at home). EM melts: EM+O=NO, EM+A=NA: ESTOU NO BANCO (at the bank), NA PRAÇA (at the square). Esquerda (left), direita (right), em frente (ahead)!

grammar.title: ESTAR + em/no/na
grammar.explain: ESTOU = I am, ESTÁ = you/he/she is. EM + O = NO (no banco), EM + A = NA (na praça). ESTOU NO HOTEL = I am at the hotel.
mistakes: Saying SOU em casa — location is always ESTAR.
Saying EM O banco — melt it: NO banco.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?
It is over there, on the right.
Is it far?
No, it is near. Five minutes.

lessons.title: Travel and pretérito (simple past)
lessons.learn: Finished trips use PRETÉRITO PERFEITO: VIAJEI (I travelled), VIAJOU (you/he/she travelled). -AR verbs: -EI (eu), -OU (você/ele/ela). FALEI, COMPROU, CHEGOU!

grammar.title: Past -AR: viajei, viajou
grammar.explain: Drop -AR, add -EI (I), -OU (você/ele/ela). VIAJEI = I travelled. COMPROU = you/he/she bought. ONTEM (yesterday) loves this past!
mistakes: Saying VIAJO for the past — past I = VIAJEI.
Forgetting ONTEM goes with finished past, not present.

dialogue.en: Did you travel this summer?

dialogue.t: Sim, viajei para o México. Visitei a praia.
dialogue.r: seeng, vee-ah-ZHAY pah-rah oo MEH-shee-koo. vee-zee-TAY ah PRAH-yah.
dialogue.en: Yes, I travelled to Mexico. I visited the beach.
Did you like it?
I loved it!

lessons.title: Direções: a pé, de ônibus, de metrô
lessons.learn: Brazilian directions are given in the imperative you (vira, desce, pega), which is the same form as the third person singular: ele vira, você vira. Distance is counted in quadras (blocks) and walking time, and the destination is placed with fica: fica a duas quadras daqui.

grammar.title: Giving and following directions
grammar.pattern: vira à direita · desce na próxima · fica a duas quadras daqui
grammar.explain: The tu/você imperative is the ordinary spoken form: vira, desce, sobe, pega, segue. Landmarks come before the direction (depois do mercado, vira à esquerda), and the answer to quanto tempo a pé? is given in minutes: uns dez minutos.

examples.t: Segue reto e vira à direita depois do mercado.
examples.r: SEH-gee HEH-too ee VEE-rah ah jee-RAY-tah deh-POYS doo mehr-KAH-doo.
examples.en: Go straight and turn right after the market.

examples.t: A estação fica a duas quadras daqui.
examples.r: ah es-tah-SOW(n) FEE-kah ah DOO-ahs KWAH-drahs dah-KEE.
examples.en: The station is two blocks from here.

examples.t: Pega o ônibus no ponto em frente à farmácia.
examples.r: PEH-gah oo OH-nee-boos noo POHN-too ey(n) FREHN-jee ah fahr-MAH-see-ah.
examples.en: Take the bus at the stop opposite the pharmacy.

mistakes.why: Direction uses the preposition a: à direita.

mistakes.wrong: O ponto fica a duas quadras longe.
mistakes.right: O ponto fica a duas quadras daqui.
mistakes.why: Distance from here is daqui, not longe.

dialogue.t: Desculpe, como eu chego ao museu?
dialogue.r: des-KOOL-pee, KOH-moo eh-oo SHEH-goo ah-oo moo-ZEH-oo?
dialogue.en: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?

dialogue.t: Segue reto até o semáforo e vira à esquerda.
dialogue.r: SEH-gee HEH-too ah-TEH oo seh-MAH-foh-roo ee VEE-rah ah es-KEHR-dah.
dialogue.en: Go straight to the traffic light and turn left.

dialogue.t: É longe? Dá para ir a pé?
dialogue.r: eh LOHN-jee? dah pah-rah eer ah PEH?
dialogue.en: Is it far? Can I walk?

dialogue.t: Dá. Uns quinze minutos, ou duas quadras de metrô.
dialogue.r: dah. oo(n)s KEEN-zee mee-NOO-toos, oh DOO-ahs KWAH-drahs jee meh-TROH.
dialogue.en: You can. About fifteen minutes, or two stops by metro.

lessons.title: Daily routines (reflexive verbs)
lessons.learn: Routines bounce back: ME LEVANTO = I get (myself) up. ME = myself, SE = yourself/himself/herself (você!). Mornings run on ME/SE: levantar-se, banhar-se, vestir-se!

grammar.title: Reflexive ME/SE: me levanto
grammar.explain: LEVANTAR-SE = to get up. ME LEVANTO (I get up), SE LEVANTA (você/he/she gets up). The little word points back — don't drop it!

examples.en: Do you bathe in the morning?

mistakes: Saying LEVANTO without ME — it means 'I lift', not 'I get up'!
Saying TE (Portugal) in Brazil — Brazil uses SE for você.

dialogue.t: A que horas você se levanta?
dialogue.r: ah kee OH-rahsh voh-SEH see leh-VAHN-tah?
dialogue.en: What time do you get up?

dialogue.t: Me levanto às sete e tomo banho.
dialogue.r: mee leh-VAHN-too ahsh SEH-chee ee TOH-moo BAH-nyoo.
dialogue.en: I get up at seven and shower.
And do you eat breakfast?
Yes, with my family.

lessons.title: Health and future (vou + verb)
lessons.learn: At the doctor: MINHA CABEÇA DÓI = my head hurts. Future with IR: VOU VIAJAR = I am going to travel. VOU, VAI + verb. The plan verb never changes!

grammar.title: Future: vou/vai + verb
grammar.explain: VOU = I go, VAI = you/he/she goes. VOU + verb = I am going to…: VOU COMER = I am going to eat. The second verb never changes!
mistakes: Changing the second verb: VOU VIAJAR, never VOU VIAJO.
Saying EU VAI — I go is VOU.

dialogue.en: Doctor, my head hurts.
Do you have a fever?
No, but I am going to rest.
Good. You are going to be fine.

lessons.title: Marcar e remarcar por telefone
lessons.learn: On the phone, the polite opening is fixed: Alô, é a Marina? and Queria marcar um horário. Queria (I wanted) is the standard soft request — it is not a past tense, it is politeness. To move an appointment, vou ter que remarcar states the problem without apologising twice, and pode ser na terça? proposes the new time.

grammar.title: Booking an appointment
grammar.pattern: Queria marcar um horário · pode ser na terça? · vou ter que remarcar
grammar.explain: Queria + infinitive is the polite request used at every counter and call centre. To offer a time, use pode ser: pode ser às duas? To accept, fica bom / para mim serve. Vou ter que + infinitive announces an unavoidable change.

examples.t: Alô, queria marcar um horário para sexta.
examples.r: ah-LOH, keh-REE-ah mahr-KAHR oo(n) oh-RAH-ree-oo pah-rah SEHS-tah.
examples.en: Hello, I'd like to book a time for Friday.

examples.t: Pode ser às três da tarde?
examples.r: POH-jee sehr ahs treys dah TAHR-jee?
examples.en: Could it be at three in the afternoon?

examples.t: Vou ter que remarcar; aconteceu um imprevisto.
examples.r: voh teh(r) kee heh-mahr-KAHR; ah-koh(n)-teh-SEH-oo oo(n) eem-preh-VEES-too.
examples.en: I'll have to reschedule; something came up.

mistakes.why: Queria is the polite form at a counter; quero sounds like a demand.
Days take em + a: na terça, na sexta.

lessons.title: Clothes and shopping (este/esse)
lessons.learn: Shop in Portuguese! A CAMISA, OS SAPATOS. Point with ESTE (this, near me) and ESSE (that, near you): ESTA CAMISA (this shirt), ESSE VESTIDO (that dress).

grammar.title: ESTE vs ESSE: this vs that
grammar.explain: ESTE/ESTA = this (near me). ESSE/ESSA = that (near you). They match gender: ESTA camisa, ESSE vestido, ESSA loja. (AQUELE = far from both!)
grammar.pattern: este/esta + near thing · esse/essa + your thing
mistakes: Saying ESTE camisa — camisa is feminine: ESTA camisa.
Using ESSE for things in your hand — near you is ESTE.

dialogue.en: How much is this shirt?

And that dress?

lessons.title: Weather scenes (fazia, havia)
lessons.learn: Weather stories use IMPERFEITO: FAZIA SOL (it was sunny), HAVIA VENTO (there was wind). Just two phrases paint any past sky!

grammar.title: First imperfeito: fazia, havia
grammar.explain: FAZIA SOL/FRIO/CALOR = it was sunny/cold/hot. HAVIA + noun = there was…: HAVIA SOL (there was sun). Weather past = imperfeito, always!
mistakes: Saying FEZ SOL for scenes — weather stories use FAZIA.
Saying HÁ for past — past needs HAVIA.

lessons.title: Pesos, medidas e troco
lessons.learn: At a Brazilian counter the request is me vê: me vê meio quilo de tomate. Quantity comes before the item, and the price is asked with quanto deu? or quanto é?. The troco is what comes back, and o troco está certo says it without counting in public. Decimals are said with e: nove e cinquenta.

grammar.title: Buying by weight
grammar.pattern: me vê meio quilo de … · quanto deu? · fica nove e cinquenta
grammar.explain: Me vê + quantity + de + item is the everyday market request. The seller answers with fica or dá: fica nove e cinquenta. A sacola, por favor asks for a bag; Brazilians often bring their own. For a fraction, meio quilo, um quarto, duzentos gramas.

examples.t: Me vê meio quilo de tomate, por favor.
examples.r: mee VEH MAY-oo KEE-loo jee toh-MAH-jee, pohr fah-VOHR.
examples.en: Can I have half a kilo of tomatoes, please?
How much did it all come to?

examples.t: Fica nove e cinquenta. Precisa de sacola?
examples.r: FEE-kah NOH-vee ee seen-KWEHN-tah. preh-SEE-zah jee sah-KOH-lah?
examples.en: That's nine fifty. Do you need a bag?

mistakes.wrong: Me vê meio quilo de tomates.
mistakes.right: Me vê meio quilo de tomate.
mistakes.why: After a quantity with de, the item stays in the singular.
One question word: quanto deu or quanto é, not both.

culture.text: Brazilian daily life runs through small shared places: the padaria at the corner, where people buy pão francês by weight (trezentos gramas, por favor) and drink a cafezinho standing at the counter; the feira on a fixed weekday, with hortifruti, pastel and caldo de cana; and the ônibus or metrô that decides how far a job can be. Prices are in reais, and the plural is regular — um real, dois reais. Food vocabulary is a survival kit rather than a menu: arroz e feijão is the plate under everything, and marmita is the box people carry to work.

reading.text: No sábado eu acordei cedo e fui à feira com a minha vizinha. Compramos banana, tomate e um quilo de laranja. Ela pediu trezentos gramas de queijo e pagou com dinheiro; eu paguei com o cartão porque não tinha troco. Depois tomamos caldo de cana em pé, perto da barraca do pastel. Voltamos a pé porque a feira fica a duas quadras da nossa rua, e chegamos em casa antes do meio-dia.
reading.gloss: On Saturday I woke up early and went to the street market with my neighbour. We bought bananas, tomatoes and a kilo of oranges. She asked for three hundred grams of cheese and paid in cash; I paid by card because I had no change. Afterwards we drank sugar-cane juice standing up, near the pastel stall. We walked back because the market is two blocks from our street, and we got home before noon.

listening.script: Boa tarde, tem pão francês? — Tem, sim. Quantos? — Quatro, por favor. E um café com leite. — Para levar? — Não, para tomar aqui. Quanto é? — Nove reais e cinquenta. — Aceita cartão? — Aceita, sim.
listening.gloss: Good afternoon, do you have French bread? — Yes, we do. How many? — Four, please. And a coffee with milk. — To take away? — No, to drink here. How much is it? — Nine reais and fifty. — Do you take card? — Yes, we do.

idioms.meaning: we — the everyday form; it takes a third-person singular verb
to sort something out, to find a way around a problem
to keep an eye on something
to be the one who takes the blame
to help someone out of a small jam
today's special — o prato do dia on any restaurant board

mistakes.why: A finished time needs the past: fui.

mistakes.wrong: Ele gosta de ler e eu gosto também de ler livros.
mistakes.right: Ele gosta de ler e eu também gosto de ler livros.
mistakes.why: The adverb também sits before the verb it shares.
pagar keeps the gu in the first person: paguei.

task.title: Lista da feira e um diálogo
task.instructions: Write a market list of eight items with quantities in Portuguese (quilo, gramas, dúzia), then write the six-line dialogue you would have at the counter: ask for two items, ask the price, ask whether they take card, and say thank you. Read it out loud once without looking.
